author: reek
body: Ties the machine's ears to its voice: it BEEPS to ask for a sound, then listens for several seconds and reports whether it heard anything. The beep is the cue -- you do not have to be watching the console. Skipped in the battery (needs a real microphone and speaker, and a person to answer). Run it by hand:

author: reek
body: The row says [Microphone, Audio] because this program does both: it speaks and it listens. It used to say [Device.Mmio] for the beep, which granted the whole Device family -- the bus and the block device -- to a program whose entire ambition was one note. Two narrow authorities that name what it actually does is the point.
